records.locator: read-configuration over a configuration authoring `name: null` / `forwardPorts: []` / `containerEnv: {}` and omitting `mounts`
records.summary: Whether a resolved-configuration result distinguishes an authored null, an authored empty collection, and an omitted property.
With an explicit --config pointing at a nonexistent file, the reference CLI rejects (no silent discovery fallback).

records.locator: com.docker.compose.project.config_files / config-hash on a Compose-backed workspace
records.summary: How each CLI delivers its generated Compose override, and the Compose labels derived from the resulting file set.
The reference CLI derives the compose project name as <folder>_devcontainer verbatim, which can be invalid (e.g. leading separators) or collide with deacon's project.

The reference emits `{"$mid": 1, "fsPath": <abs>, "path": <abs>, "scheme": "vscode-fileHost"}` on both documents, with `fsPath` and `path` identical and always absolute regardless of how the workspace folder was named on the command line. Observed 2026-07-28 over all 80 comparable conformance fixtures.

On the same fixture (fx-up-basic, image alpine:3.19), `docker inspect .Config.Labels` shows the reference CLI setting exactly three labels — devcontainer.metadata, devcontainer.local_folder, devcontainer.config_file — while deacon sets those three plus five it alone defines: devcontainer.configHash, devcontainer.config_name, devcontainer.name, devcontainer.source (value "deacon"), devcontainer.workspaceHash. devcontainer.metadata is byte-identical between the two; local_folder and config_file differ only by each side's own workspace path.

`docker inspect .Config.Cmd` on fx-up-container-labels shows two different shell keep-alive strings. Behavioral equivalence measured by `docker stop` wall time and exit code: deacon 245 ms / exit 0, reference 215 ms / exit 0.

The reference CLI accepts an object with a duplicate top-level key and applies last-wins.
The reference CLI v0.87.0 does not resolve extends; --include-merged-configuration errors with 'No image information specified'.

The reference CLI does not resolve extends at read-configuration, so an extends pointing at a nonexistent file is accepted (echoed literally).

Both CLIs place a dependency before its dependant in the resolved Feature set; the reported documents differ in shape, the reference additionally reporting process-local cache paths and consecutive ids (observed 2026-07-26).
The reference CLI recovers from a hard JSONC syntax error by dropping the broken property and accepting the file.
With no devcontainer configuration present at all, the reference CLI rejects rather than inventing an empty config.

The reference emits exactly `workspaceFolder` and `workspaceMount`. Observed 2026-07-28 across a plain workspace, a git-subdirectory workspace, a git-subdirectory workspace with an explicit `workspaceFolder`, and a compose workspace; the mount target stayed `/workspaces/<basename(source)>` in every case, including the one whose `workspaceFolder` was `/opt/app`.
